items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18
items.q: It was a big, it was a fairly big band for those days. Did you play in that band yourself? Yeah.

ctx.x: Yeah. Now, Marge wasn't with Charlie Crefft at that time, was it?

Well, no, I wouldn't know. You know Marge? Yeah, yeah. His sister? I wouldn't, I wouldn't know. Who married Zuri? Yeah, yeah. No. I don't know, because I never met, uh, I didn't meet his wife, uh, in fact, I can't even remember one guy that was in that band. Hmm. It was a big, it was a fairly big band for those days. Did you play in that band yourself? Yeah. It was about, uh, uh, nine or ten pieces. They had two, three saxophones in that band, and you read everything then.
You read it? Oh, yeah. In Charlie Crefft's band? Yeah. For the reading band? Well, sure. Nine or ten pieces? Naturally.

items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: In the whole length of time I probably only played with him off and on maybe for four weeks.

ctx.x: Somehow I got the feeling that you lived there and played Charlie Creath.
Well, I played with Charlie, although I still played with the medicine show.
Well, let me ask you a little bit about Charlie Creath and all that kind of business in St. Louis. Was Charlie the number-one band in St. Louis?
